bihar_raw_news.content: Patna: Expelled JD(U) leader and Mokama MLA Anant Kumar Singh on Sunday claimed the party would struggle to win even 10-12 seats in future elections and announced plans to float his own political outfit. Expulsion Follows Feud With Party Colleague Singh made the remarks a day after the JD(U) expelled him for six years over alleged anti-party activities. He said he had no regrets over the action. The action against Singh followed his repeated public attacks on party colleague and MLC Neeraj Kumar during the recent Bihar Legislative Council elections. Instead of supporting Neeraj, contesting the election from the Patna Graduates' constituency, Anant supported Jan Suraaj Party (JSP)-backed candidate Anuj Singh. Before Anant Singh's expulsion from the party, former JD(U) president Rajiv Ranjan Singh alias Lalan Singh had held deliberations with former chief minister and party chief Nitish Kumar. Lalan Singh had earlier attempted to broker peace between Anant Singh and Neeraj Kumar, both of whom belong to the politically influential Bhumihar community. However, the reconciliation efforts failed to end the public feud. Banks have been asked to clear pending loan applications, reduce rejection rates and achieve their targets in mission mode. The directives were issued during the third review meeting of a high-level committee held at the Old Secretariat on Friday under the chairmanship of Development Commissioner Mihir Kumar Singh . The meeting reviewed the overall performance of banks, progress under the Annual Credit Plan, the credit-deposit (CD) ratio and lending under various government welfare schemes. During the meeting, Singh introduced a 100-point scientific measurement index to assess the performance of banks operating in Bihar. The new system is intended to establish a transparent framework for scoring and ranking banks against specified parameters. The state government has also incorporated four additional welfare schemes into its credit-monitoring mechanism to improve oversight of financial flows. Against the Annual Credit Plan target of Rs 4.95 lakh crore, banks disbursed Rs 1,89,343 crore by the end of the September quarter, achieving 38.25 per cent of the annual target. This represented an increase of Rs 46,228 crore compared with the corresponding period of 2025-26, according to the figures presented at the meeting. The MSME sector recorded credit disbursement of Rs 84,091 crore against a target of Rs 1,59,632 crore, achieving 52.68 per cent of its target. In agriculture, banks extended Rs 43,967.17 crore against a target of Rs 1,57,015 crore, representing 28 per cent achievement. Overall priority-sector lending reached Rs 1,30,619 crore against a target of Rs 3,55,532 crore, or 36.74 per cent. Bihar's CD ratio stood at 60.21 per cent at the end of the 2025-26 financial year and was recorded at 60.17 per cent on September 30. bihar_raw_news.content: Advertisement Home / National / Bihar to develop Rs 16,500-crore manufacturing city in Gayaji, to generate 1.1 lakh jobs Bihar to develop Rs 16,500-crore manufacturing city in Gayaji, to generate 1.1 lakh jobs GAYAJI (Bihar), Oct 24 : Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Saturday unveiled the logo and portal of a 1,670-acre manufacturing city in Gayaji, with an estimated investment potential of Rs 16,500 crore and over 1.1 lakh jobs. Speaking on... Daily Excelsior 04:23 AM Oct 25, 2026 IST GAYAJI (Bihar), Oct 24 : Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Saturday unveiled the logo and portal of a 1,670-acre manufacturing city in Gayaji, with an estimated investment potential of Rs 16,500 crore and over 1.1 lakh jobs. Speaking on the occasion, Choudhary said the state government was focused on attracting investments, strengthening infrastructure and creating employment opportunities for local youth. Choudhary said Bihar was fully prepared for industrial growth, with large-scale efforts underway to promote industrial investment, infrastructure development, air connectivity and employment generation. Advertisement He urged investors from across the country and abroad to recognise the opportunities available in the state. "The Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City in Gaya is being developed across approximately 1,670 acres in Dobhi block under the Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC). The project has an estimated investment potential of Rs 16,500 crore and is expected to generate around 1.1 lakh jobs", the CM said. "The government is also pursuing land acquisition across approximately 13,500 acres for industrial and infrastructure development, which is expected to be completed by January next year. A township and cultural heritage centre named after Magadh are also planned to promote tourism and economic activity", the CM said. Choudhary said plans were underway to connect Gaya to Dubai and Kathmandu by air, while efforts would be made to expand air connectivity to Bhagalpur, Sonepur and other locations. Identifying sectors such as steel, textiles, food processing, electronics, electric vehicles and biofuels as key investment opportunities, he said the government would focus on converting investment commitments into operational projects and jobs. The chief minister also urged the Bihari diaspora to contribute to the state's development, noting that Bihar Foundation had established connections with people in 55 countries. Industries Department Secretary Kundan Kumar announced that Bihar Business Connect 2027 would be held on February 17 and 18. Meanwhile, the state government also signed MoUs with 12 industrial units involving proposed investments of Rs 4,092 crore in the presence of the CM at the event. The proposed investments cover energy, textiles, organic products, automobiles, aluminium, agro-based industries and biotechnology, and are expected to boost industrial production and generate employment. Union Minister Jitan Ram Manjhi, Deputy Chief Ministers Vijay Kumar Choudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav, state ministers, Ambassadors of Japan, Thailand and Laos, Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit, senior state and district officials, industrialists, investors and other dignitaries were also present. bihar_raw_news.content: Related News Bihar: PNG service reaches Buxar's Dumraon, beneficiaries count benefits of piped c... Electronics emerges as India`s 'new oil' as trade deficit nears $40 billion Nagaland has potential to emerge as major producer of premium coffee: Governor Centre asks states to help in speeding up switch from LPG to PNG by households Russian crude imports increase to 41 pc, supply secured till July: BPCL Domestic LPG supply normal, 4.58 lakh new PNG connections gasified 2026-10-25 09:07:19 am | Source: IANS Bihar: PNG service reaches Buxar's Dumraon, beneficiaries count benefits of piped cooking gas News By Tags | #Industry #Commodity #Bihar #CookingGas #Dumraon #PNG #AnkitKumar #IndianOil The residents of Dumraon in Buxar district of Bihar are a happy lot as they have received a Diwali bonanza ahead of the festive celebrations. The Piped Natural Gas (PNG) connection has reached their village, giving them an opportunity for uninterrupted cooking gas supply while removing daily hassles of booking LPG cylinders, managing deliveries and also the physical effort of transporting them to respective households. The PNG service was unveiled in the Textile Colony of Dumraon by the District Magistrate. Under the new system, gas will be supplied directly to household kitchens via pipeline. Plans are also in place to expand this service to Buxar city and other areas in the near future. The introduction of prepaid PNG service in the Textile Colony of Dumraon offers consumers an alternative, reducing their reliance on traditional gas cylinders. The facility was inaugurated by District Magistrate Sahila Heer. On this occasion, District Magistrate Sahila Heer mentioned that PNG service would be expanded to other parts of the district. The initiative aims to extend the pipeline network to Buxar city as well as various rural areas in the near future. ''First of all, I would like to congratulate all the IOCL representatives for installing PNG connections here in record time. A total of 498 technically feasible households have been provided with PNG connections, and today, we have inaugurated the service at one household,” the DM Sahila Heer said. Ankit Kumar, Senior Manager (CGD) at Indian Oil , and a resident, Pooja Jha, also shared their perspectives on the new facility. “We have provided connections to five households here, and we plan to supply gas through pipelines to all technically feasible households in Dumraon that meet PNGRB standards in the coming days,'' he stated. The beneficiaries noted that the PNG connection ensures a direct supply of gas to their kitchens, offering greater convenience. They described it as both a practical and cost-effective option. The direct delivery of a piped gas connection offers consumers many conveniences and comforts that existed never before. bihar_raw_news.title: NICDC launches Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City Gaya Limited, signs 12 MoUs worth Rs ...
bihar_raw_news.content: NICDC launches Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City Gaya Limited, signs 12 MoUs worth Rs 4,200 crore ANI | Updated: Oct 25, 2026 08:09 IST ANI News Join our Whatsapp channel New Delhi [India], October 25 (ANI): The National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) has launched Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City Gaya Limited (BIMCGL), signing 12 Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) covering approximately 300 acres of land with proposed investments worth Rs 4,200 crore at Integrated Manufacturing City (IMC) Gaya, as per a statement by the Ministry of Commerce & Industry. The company was formally launched by Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary at Bodh Gaya on Saturday. The event also witnessed the curtain raiser for Bihar Business Connect 2027, the Ministry said. According to the release, BIMCGL is the Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV) tasked with implementing the Integrated Manufacturing Cluster (IMC) at Gaya under the Amritsar–Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC), part of the National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP). “The National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) marked a significant milestone in advancing industrial development in Bihar with the formal launch of Bihar Integrated Manufacturing City Gaya Limited (BIMCGL) by the Chief Minister of Bihar, Shri Samrat Choudhary, at Bodh Gaya,” the release said. Spread across 1,670 acres in the Dobhi block of Gaya district, the project was approved by the Centre on August 28, 2024, at a total cost of Rs 1,339 crore, including land acquisition costs. “It is expected to attract investments of approximately Rs 16,500 crore and generate employment opportunities for around 1.10 lakh people,” the release said. Incorporated on January 6, 2025, BIMCGL is a joint venture between the Bihar Industrial Area Development Authority (BIADA) and the National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT), with both holding equal equity stakes. “As the dedicated implementing agency, BIMCGL will expedite project execution through coordinated planning, infrastructure development, statutory clearances, utility connectivity and investor facilitation,” the Ministry said, adding, “The institutional framework will enable faster decision-making, effective monitoring and timely resolution of implementation-related issues.” Infrastructure development at IMC Gaya is underway, with the Bihar government taking possession of the entire project land. The Centre released the first equity tranche of Rs 132 crore in September 2025 against the transfer of 415 acres. Project management consultants and an EPC contractor for trunk infrastructure works have been appointed, while physical construction has commenced. Construction of a dedicated helipad at IMC Gaya is also at an advanced stage to improve accessibility for investors, business delegations and senior officials. The industrial cluster will feature integrated infrastructure, including roads, water supply, sewerage and wastewater treatment facilities, power distribution, solid waste management and fire safety systems. Located near NH-22 and NH-19, with Gaya Airport approximately 39 km away, the project offers connectivity to major industrial and commercial centres. Furthermore, “IMC Gaya will focus on sectors including agro-based industries, textiles and readymade garments, furniture, handicrafts and handloom, and engineering and fabrication. The planned infrastructure will support large manufacturers and MSMEs, encourage local entrepreneurship and strengthen industrial value chains across the region,”

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi Inaugurates RBI Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Odisha
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India’s Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute at Info Valley-II in Jatni, near Bhubaneswar, Odisha. Speaking on the occasion, the Prime Minister said the project would be immensely beneficial for the people of Odisha and the country. He congratulated everyone associated with the project. Mr. Modi said that development, for the government, means ensuring balanced growth across India by creating opportunities in villages and smaller towns. He emphasized the importance of improving connectivity in even the most remote areas, enabling poor families to live with dignity, and ensuring that no citizen is left behind in the country’s development journey. The Prime Minister also said that India’s banking sector has become one of the most efficient in the world, with people now having access to banking services round the clock. Prime Minister Modi arrived in Odisha capital after completing his visit to Varanasi, in Uttar Pradesh. He was welcomed by Governor Braj Mohan Ram, Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi and other dignitaries at the Jatni helipad. Built at an estimated cost of around 170 crore rupees, the data centre is expected to strengthen the security of critical financial data and enhance the resilience of India’s digital financial infrastructure. It will support mission-critical systems, including payment and settlement operations of the Reserve Bank. The accompanying Cybersecurity Training Institute will provide specialised training and promote research in cybersecurity, enterprise computing and emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence and quantum computing. The facility is expected to strengthen the RBI’s technological capabilities and contribute to the security, reliability and resilience of the country’s rapidly expanding digital financial ecosystem.

national_raw_news.title: IMD Issues Red Alert for Five Odisha Districts Ahead of Cyclonic Storm 55 mins ago 25
national_raw_news.content: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning and further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm before reaching the Andhra Pradesh coast on Wednesday. The IMD has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall in Odisha from Tuesday to Thursday, with five southern districts facing a red warning. The Odisha Government has mobilised disaster response teams, ordered precautionary measures and prioritised the safety of people in vulnerable areas. “The deep depression over the east-central and adjoining southeast Bay of Bengal is moving towards the Indian east coast and is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) forecasts further intensification into a severe cyclonic storm on Tuesday and a very severe cyclonic storm by Wednesday. The system is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam by the Wednesday forenoon, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 115 to 125 kilometres per hour and gusts reaching 140 kilometres per hour. In Odisha, heavy to very heavy rainfall is forecast from Tuesday through Thursday. Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri are among the districts facing heightened risks, with a red warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall on Wednesday. Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has directed the administration to ensure preparedness and minimise casualties. Around 60 ODRAF teams and 17 NDRF teams have been deployed, while 225 Fire Services teams remain on high alert. Schools, colleges and Anganwadi centres in the five southern districts will remain closed on Wednesday and Thursday. Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the sea, while authorities are preparing for evacuations and possible disruption to transport, power supply and agricultural activities.

national_raw_news.title: Next wave of retail broking to come from towns, villages, says SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey 24 Oct 2026 | 7:59 PM 269
national_raw_news.content: SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey today said that the next wave in retail broking will not come from the big cities alone but will come from towns and villages. Addressing the 16th International Capital Market Convention of Association of NSE Members of India – ANMI, Mr. Pandey said, the best brokers do not just execute trades, they guide. Stating that KYC must be treated as “Know Your Client’s Needs”, SEBI Chairman said a client who understands risks invests wisely and stays invested longer. He further encouraged brokers to introduce investors to choices beyond equity like a bond, or a unit of a REIT or an InvIT. Raising serious concerns that about six in ten investors rely on unregistered advisers and so-called influencers, Mr. Pandey said SEBI’s campaign “Samajh Se Investing Simple” has drawn over 15 crore views on social media and sent close to 110 crore WhatsApp messages since its launch on 5th October. Urging market participants to treat cyber security as a business priority, not an IT expense, the SEBI chief said a single breach can shake trust across the system. Stating that the International Monetary Fund – IMF expects India to grow at about 7 percent this year, which is more than twice the global pace, Mr. Pandey said, the prediction is largely due to the country’s young population, large domestic market and steady reforms. He informed that India’s equity market capitalization stands around 470 lakh crore rupees while Mutual Fund Assets Under Management – AUM stand around 83 lakh crore rupees. With over 15 crore unique investors and a foreign portfolio investor assets of about 74 lakh crore rupees, Mr. Pandey said the aim is to keep building a market that is simpler, deeper and safer, for investors and for market participants. In that direction, the SEBI Chief said, the regulator is reviewing short selling and securities lending and borrowing to improve liquidity and price discovery. He added that a framework is being developed to lift secondary trading in corporate bonds and another to put in place safeguards to prevent misuse of trading terminals. Mr. Pandey said SEBI is also exploring an AI sandbox, where new tools can be tested safely.

national_raw_news.title: CRPF Takes Over Sinai Camp of Kuki Militant Group in Manipur 3 hours ago 72
national_raw_news.content: In Manipur, Sinai Camp, which is a camp of Kuki militant group under Suspension of Operation (SoO) with the Government, has been disarmed and taken over by the CRPF. A team of security forces, including Manipur Police, CoBRA Unit of CRPF and other agencies, conducted a joint operation at the Sinai Camp located in Kangpokpi district recently after three innocent Meitei civilians were killed in an ambush near the camp. During the operation, 17 individuals impersonating registered SoO cadres using false identities were found only in the camp, which is supposed to house about 150 cadres. The camp was the designated camp of the Kuki National Army (KNA) and Kuki Liberation Army (KLA), which are under the Suspension of Operation (SoO) agreement. Manipur Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh today visited the camp and inspected the entire camp premises and was briefed by officers of the CRPF and Assam Rifles on the operation conducted and the prevailing law and order situation in the area. While interacting with senior security officers and personnel, the Chief Minister commended the CRPF’s CoBRA Battalion for its courage and valour, particularly for its leading role in the successful operation that led to total control of the camp. He maintained that due care must be taken to ensure innocent civilians are not affected by combing operations. MLA Thokchom Radheshyam, senior officers of CRPF, Manipur Police, and Assam Rifles were also present during the visit.

national_raw_news.title: ‘India expresses global sentiment when it urges that dialogue and diplomacy are only soluti...
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar has said that India expresses global sentiment when it urges that dialogue and diplomacy are the only solution for conflicts. He said, India is making efforts itself and is open to working with other partners to that end. Speaking at the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan this morning in New Delhi, Dr Jaishankar said, there are two major conflicts going on today in the world in Ukraine and in West Asia. He said, societies and economies, peoples far away, who have little say in the matter, are actually paying the cost. Dr Jaishankar underlined that terrorism is another deadly threat to peace. He said, its usage as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable, it can never be justified and can never be rationalized. The Minister pointed out that terrorism continues because not all states really display zero tolerance. He expressed concern that despite history holding so many lessons, some states still allow political calculations to take precedence. Dr Jaishankar said, the world must therefore develop sharper awareness about this common threat and must come together with stronger resolve to counter terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. He said, progress and prosperity are the flip side of conflict and violence and they too are equally indivisible. The Minister said, the world cannot advance half prosperous and half denied in an era of intricate supply chains, of globalized markets, and of common resources. He said, this is simply a prescription for continuous instability. The Minister said, the Global South today faces a 4F crisis of finance, fuel, food, and fertilizer. He said, the Global North must realize that it has equal stakes in finding solutions. Dr Jaishankar said, the international economy must be urgently de-risked and nations provided with more diversified options. He said, market distortions through constriction and choke points only add to suffering. He added that a genuine dialogue in this regard is overdue. Dr Jaishankar said, progress is understandably associated with the march of technology and humankind now really stands at the crossroads. He said, AI promises to be the mother of all change, but something so sweeping and consequential cannot be left in the hands of just a few. The External Affairs Minister further stated that it will go counter to the trends of freedom and democratization that the world has seen over the last 80 years. He said, for this reason, India is a strong advocate of a responsible, inclusive, and human-centric approach. He added that it is a recognition of AI’s universal applicability and of the need to develop a wider perspective.

national_raw_news.title: India slams Pakistan at UN on Minority Rights Violations and Military Control
national_raw_news.content: India criticised Pakistan at the United Nations, accusing Islamabad of attempting to malign New Delhi through propaganda while diverting attention from its domestic challenges, including economic distress, lawlessness and human rights violations. Speaking during an interactive dialogue with the Special Rapporteur on Minority Issues at the UN General Assembly’s Third Committee yesterday, India’s First Secretary to the UN, Raghoo Puri, questioned Pakistan’s record on minority rights and alleged that the country’s military continued to exercise decisive control over its political leadership. Referring to the controversy surrounding Pakistan’s 2024 general elections, Puri described Islamabad’s administration as a ‘Form 47 government’ and said it could not override the instructions of the Pakistani military, which he called the country’s ‘real rulers’. Form 47 is an official election document in Pakistan that records the provisional, consolidated results of voting in a constituency. Puri also highlighted concerns over the shrinking minority population in Pakistan and urged Islamabad to focus on the welfare of its own citizens rather than criticising India at international forums. Rejecting Pakistan’s claims on Jammu and Kashmir, he reiterated that the region was an integral part of India and said the outstanding issue was the vacation of territories under Pakistan’s illegal occupation. Defending India’s record on minority rights, Puri described the country as a multi-religious, multi-ethnic and multilingual society, highlighting constitutional safeguards and the contributions of minority communities across government, the armed forces, industry and culture. Puri also stressed that protecting minority rights was primarily the sovereign responsibility of individual countries.

national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today said Mann Ki Baat has completed 12 years and that the journey has felt like a pilgrimage for him. Addressing the nation through his Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani, the Prime Minister noted that Mann Ki Baat began on the auspicious occasion of Vijayadashami 12 years ago. Since then, this journey has continued without a break. The Prime Minister said that the listeners of Mann Ki Baat are both his fellow travellers and guides. He further said that Mann Ki Baat has been an auspicious opportunity to proudly celebrate the hard work, valour, commitment, dedication, and spirit of service of the common people of the nation. Mr. Modi added that this has been like a Teerth Yatra (pilgrimage trip) to closely understand the efforts of the people and to salute their contributions. He said people who live for society and the nation are, in themselves, like a ‘Teerth’ (Pilgrimage). He also said that through Mann Ki Baat, he is paying obeisance to the collective strength of the people of India. The Prime Minister said that Mann Ki Baat provides him with an opportunity to connect with every family across the country. He said this deep connection and the affection shown by all of the listeners is a priceless treasure. Saying that the nation possesses many traditional skills that have been a part of its identity for generations, Prime Minister Modi highlighted an initiative underway in Punjab. An organisation called ‘Kheti Virasat Mission’ has begun to breathe new life into organic farming and traditional agricultural practices. The team aimed to promote natural cotton cultivation in the Malwa region of Punjab, with the initiative named ‘Nav-Trinjan’. Under this project, organic cotton with natural colours is cultivated, eliminating the need for additional chemicals to dye the resulting yarn or fabric. ‘Nav-Trinjan’ also established a weaving school with the goal of passing on the craft of weaving to the next generation. Mr Modi mentioned how Ramandeep Kaur, a labourer; Suneha Devi, a domestic help and Rajni Kaur, a manual labourer are now being recognised as a skilled- weavers who are supporting their households with this new found skill. He also mentioned that a shawl woven by Rekha Rani has been presented to the President of India. He recalled meeting this team on National Handloom Day a few months ago. He extended his heartfelt wishes to the entire team for a bright future. Speaking about conservation of Nature, Mr Modi highlighted the efforts in Tehri Garhwal region of Uttarakhand to breathe new life into the ‘Heval’ river and the natural water sources in the surrounding area. He commended the local administration and the villagers who launched a campaign to save the Heval river. Measures were undertaken to capture rainwater, facilitate groundwater recharge and plant a large number of trees. Mr Modi noted with satisfaction that due to these efforts, the Heval river has been revitalised and dozens of natural water sources have received help in their restoration. The Prime Minister noted that cleanliness drives are being run at many places ahead of festivals like Diwali and Chhath. He stressed the need to maintain cleanliness of the places where people live. He added that small, individual efforts can bring about significant change in the surroundings.The Prime Minister expressed happiness that people are placing great importance on Swadeshi products while shopping during this festive season. He remarked that this spirit of ‘Vocal for Local’ is taking Indian products to global markets. He highlighted that Makhana from Purnia in Bihar is now reaching Greece, and Arhar Dal from Kalaburagi in Karnataka is being exported to the Maldives. He underlined that new global markets are opening up for Indian farmers. Mr Modi emphasised that packaging of a product is just as significant as its quality. He cited the example of tribal communities in Maharashtra who have placed a strong focus on the packaging of the products they create. Through an initiative called ‘Shabari Naturals,’ products like honey, mahua, chironji and bamboo-based items are being brought to the market with packaging which reflects their tribal art. national_raw_news.title: Low-pressure system over Bay of Bengal likely to cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam 4 hours ago 59
national_raw_news.content: The Low-pressure system over Bay of Bengal likely to cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam as very severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 115 to 125 kilometres per hour gusting to 140 kilometres per hour by forenoon of Wednesday. India Meteorological Department has forecast heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday and Wednesday and also over Odisha and Telangana on Wednesday. The India Meteorological Department has issued a pre-cyclone watch for the Andhra Pradesh and adjoining south Odisha coasts, as a depression over the Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm. The IMD has forecast heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in parts of Coastal Andhra Pradesh on October 27 and 28. Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu has directed officials to remain alert and warn people in low-lying areas. Fisheries officials are taking steps to bring fishing boats safely ashore. Power utilities are also preparing teams to restore electricity in case of disruptions. Odisha is on alert for heavy to extremely heavy rainfall, strong winds and possible flooding, as the state government steps up disaster preparedness. Akashvani correspondent reports that the Met Dept is closely monitoring a depression over the east-central Bay of Bengal, which is expected to intensify into a cyclonic storm by tomorrow morning and a severe cyclonic storm by day after tomorrow. It may further strengthen into a very severe cyclonic storm before approaching the Andhra Pradesh coast around Wednesday morning. The system was located about 860 kilometres east-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 1,130 kilometres east of Bapatla in the latest bulletin from IMD. The projected landfall zone is along the Andhra Pradesh coast, between Visakhapatnam and Bapatla, though the precise location remains subject to further updates. Odisha is likely to experience heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in several districts under the impact of the weather system. The state government has placed all districts on alert and kept disaster-response teams on standby. Fishermen have been advised to return to shore and avoid venturing into the sea. People are urged to follow official weather advisories.

national_raw_news.title: Centre achieves target of creating 11 crore Farmer IDs across the country
national_raw_news.content: The Centre has created 11 crore farmer IDs across the country, five months ahead of the March 2027 deadline. The milestone has been achieved under the Digital Agriculture Mission implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare. The Farmer ID initiative is designed to provide farmers with a unique digital identity, enabling transparent, efficient and timely access to government schemes, bank credit, crop insurance and disaster relief, while reducing paperwork and repeated verification. Agriculture and Farmers Welfare Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan said this today while sharing a video message. The Minister said that the target of creating 11 crore Farmer IDs by March 2027 was set by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and it was achieved yesterday, five months ahead of schedule. Mr Chouhan said that Farmer IDs will ensure transparent delivery of benefits under various government schemes. They will facilitate farmers in accessing bank loans, crop insurance, disaster relief assistance and selling their produce. He added that the initiative will help ensure that benefits reach the right farmers, while the use of modern technology will make farming easier and more efficient. Mr Chouhan congratulated and thanked the officials and employees of the Central Government, as well as the state governments, union territories, and district administrations, for this achievement. The Ministry added that the Digital Agriculture Mission was launched following the Union Cabinet’s approval on 2nd September, 2024. The Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) being developed under the mission is already showing results on the ground. It added that through the Farmer ID-based service delivery system, more than 6 crore farmers across the country have so far received direct benefits under various schemes. Linking a verified farmer database with agricultural services is helping eliminate fraud and the need for duplicate verification. The Ministry furhter stated that it has also improved coordination among government departments and strengthened policy formulation and the monitoring of schemes, making it easier to track their implementation and delivery of benefits.

Top Stories of the Day Share DD India October 25, 2026 8:58 AM IST PM Modi to Visit Varanasi, Bhubaneswar today; to Inaugurate Garment Facility, RBI Data Centre Author: DD India Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Uttar Pradesh and Odisha on October 25 to inaugurate a garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi, witness the Indian Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026, and inaugurate the Reserve Bank of India’s Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar. According to the Prime Minister’s Office, the Prime Minister will inaugurate Arvind Limited’s new garment manufacturing facility in Varanasi at around 11 AM. At around 1 PM, he will witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat as the Chief Guest. He will then travel to Bhubaneswar, where he is scheduled to inaugurate the RBI’s newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute at around 4:45 PM and address the gathering. Garment Manufacturing Facility in Varanasi The new garment manufacturing facility is expected to strengthen India’s textile and apparel manufacturing ecosystem and promote industrial growth in the region. The facility will adopt modern manufacturing practices and create employment opportunities, particularly for women. With a global customer base, it is expected to connect garments manufactured in Varanasi with international markets. The initiative also highlights Uttar Pradesh’s efforts to attract industrial investment, expand manufacturing capacity and promote women-led development. Indian Air Force Day Aerial Display at Namo Ghat The Prime Minister will also witness the Air Force Day Aerial Display-2026 at Namo Ghat in Varanasi. The event will commemorate the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force under the theme “Wings over Ganges”. The aerial display will feature aircraft including the Tejas, Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) Prachand, Su-30MKI and Rafale, along with transport aircraft. Aircraft from the Indian Navy and the Indian Army will also participate, highlighting jointness among the armed forces. The Indian Air Force’s Surya Kiran Aerobatic Team and Sarang Helicopter Display Team will showcase precision flying, coordination and operational capabilities. RBI Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar In Odisha, the Prime Minister will inaugurate the RBI’s new Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, aimed at strengthening the technological infrastructure supporting India’s financial system. The data centre infrastructure has been designed to provide secure, resilient, scalable and future-ready computing capabilities for the RBI and the wider financial sector. According to the release, four state-of-the-art data centres will host mission-critical payment and settlement systems, along with other key initiatives. The facility has received the Uptime Institute’s Tier IV certification, a benchmark for data centre infrastructure resilience, placing it in the highest certification tier.
